summary: Oregon lookout site under the Walker Range Patrol and a timber company: stations from 1927, staffed in 1940 and 1943, a tree crow's nest decayed by 2006.

facts.design: Tree crow's nest with a camp
facts.status_note: A 2006 entry says the tree had decayed to almost nothing, with a few boards and tin cans left; no later source
facts.agency: Walker Range Patrol / Private Timber Company

events.note: Intermediate lookout put in place because of high hazard fire weather; site near a Shevlin-Hixon logging camp
Panorama photos taken by Hunter on February 2
Walker Range Patrol staffed the lookout for 110 days; reporting station at LaPine linked by telephone
June 17, 1943 Bulletin item quoted on the page: Aleene Barton to take up the Summit Butte station as a fire lookout for the summer

evidence.supports: 1927 intermediate lookout put in place; site near a Shevlin-Hixon logging camp
evidence.quote: 1927: Due to the high hazard fire weather an intermediate lookout was put in place. This site is near a Shevlin-Hixon logging camp.
August 12, 1929: An intermediate lookout was stationed.
August 9, 1930: An emergency lookout was stationed.

evidence.supports: panorama photos taken by Hunter in February 1934
evidence.quote: February 2, 1934: Panorama photos were taken by Hunter.

evidence.supports: Walker Range Patrol staffed the lookout for 110 days in 1940; reporting station at LaPine linked by telephone
evidence.quote: 1940: The lookout was staffed by the Walker Range Patrol for 110 days. The reporting station was at LaPine and linked by telephone.

evidence.supports: 1943 summer station for Aleene Barton: to take up the Summit Butte station as a fire lookout for the summer; former residence Bend; arrived from La Grande
evidence.quote: Miss Aleene Barton, whose former residence was Bend, arrived from LaGrande, where she has been a resident, and will take up her station on Summit butte, near this camp, as a 'lookout' for fires during the summer months.

evidence.supports: date of the Bulletin item quoted for 1943
tree crow's nest with a camp; tree decayed to almost nothing by 2006
evidence.quote: A tree crow's nest with a camp. In 2006 the tree had already decayed to almost nothing, a few boards and the usual tin cans.

evidence.supports: agency given as Walker Range Patrol / Private Timber Company
evidence.quote: Walker Range Patrol / Private Timber Company

notes_for_editor: One source: the Forest Lookouts Oregon page, which lists dated entries and quotes newspapers without naming each item. No second source found. Two searches (one WebSearch, one websearch.py) and firelookout.org's Oregon list did not include this lookout. The brief's county (Klamath) and coordinates (43.4434, -121.3521) come from the site's own index and were not checked against a land record. Staffing as_of 1943 is the last date in the sources, not a current status. The 1927 entry is coded 'other' because the source says an intermediate lookout was put in place, not built. Status 'ruins' is a judgment from the 2006 entry (boards and cans remaining); no source gives a present-day state.
